facts.text: On this date in 1956, the Hungarian Revolution began — within days, 200,000 Hungarians fled across the Austrian border, the largest refugee movement in Europe since WWII.
On October 23, 1983, simultaneous truck bombs killed 241 American and 58 French peacekeepers in Beirut — still the deadliest single-day loss for the U.S. Marines since Iwo Jima.
More people live within a 40-kilometer radius of Jakarta than in the entire country of Australia.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more residents than the entire population of Canada — yet most people outside Asia have never heard of it.
Norway controls an Arctic archipelago called Svalbard where any citizen of the 46 signatory nations can live and work without a visa, making it the world's most open border zone.
On this date in 1907, the Knickerbocker Trust run began in New York, triggering a panic so severe it wiped out 50 banks — and convinced Congress that America finally needed a central bank.
On October 23, 1929, stock prices lurched violently ahead of Black Thursday, with margin calls already destroying fortunes before the crash officially had a name.
The Dutch East India Company paid dividends for 200 consecutive years. Its peak market cap, adjusted to today, exceeds $8 trillion — larger than every U.S. company combined.
Saudi Aramco once earned more per day than Apple earns per quarter. In 2022, it posted $161 billion in annual profit — the highest ever recorded by any company in history.
A standard futures contract for crude oil covers 1,000 barrels. In April 2020, traders paid $37 per barrel to give oil away — the first negative price in commodity market history.
On this date in 1947, the first X-ray of the entire human body was taken. It required 17 separate images stitched together and exposed the subject to radiation levels that would be illegal today.
On October 23, 2001, Apple launched the iPod. The same week, a Nature paper confirmed that tardigrades survive vacuum exposure by suspending every metabolic process — not slowing it, stopping it.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere 20 kilometers across. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh 10 million tons on Earth.
Your body replaces 98% of its atoms roughly every year, yet the arrangement persists. You are less a thing than a pattern — a wave that mistakes itself for water.
The universe is not merely expanding but accelerating outward. Whatever is driving this — dark energy — comprises 68% of everything, and physics has no confirmed explanation for what it actually is.
On this day in 1915, 25,000 women marched down Fifth Avenue demanding the vote — five years before the 19th Amendment passed, and the same year Einstein was finalizing general relativity.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval Europe and pre-Columbian America were strict contemporaries.
On this day in 1942, Montgomery launched El Alamein — the battle Churchill called the 'end of the beginning,' fought with maps so bad that officers sometimes navigated by stars.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, before the American Civil War. Your grandparents' office technology predates the abolition of slavery.
Woolly mammoths were still alive on Wrangel Island when the Great Pyramid was already 1,000 years old. Cleopatra is closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramid's construction.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless, shared glance between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. One of the world's hardest words to translate, from a language now spoken by a single person.
Vellichor (invented, 2013): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Coined by John Koenig for The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows — and adopted so widely it now behaves like a real word.

On this date in 1915, the first women's suffrage march down Fifth Avenue drew 25,000 marchers. The word 'suffrage' derives from Latin suffragium — a voting tablet, a broken piece of tile used as a ballot.
Sonder (invented, 2012): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Also coined by Koenig, it reads like a word that should have always existed.
Apricity: the warmth of sunlight in winter. An English word from 1623, used once in Henry Cockeram's dictionary and then abandoned — leaving a sensation perfectly named and perfectly forgotten.
On this day in 2013, the FBI seized ~174,000 BTC from Silk Road — then worth ~$33M. The government auctioned it in batches; one buyer, Tim Draper, won 30,000 BTC in a single 2014 lot.
On this day in 2021, the first U.S. Bitcoin futures ETF (ProShares BITO) launched on NYSE Arca, pulling in $1B in assets within two days — the fastest ETF to that milestone in history.
Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment recalculates every 2,016 blocks, targeting a 10-minute average. It has no price oracle — it reads only timestamps miners embed in block headers.

The Ethereum genesis block contains the hidden message 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — copied directly from Satoshi's original Bitcoin genesis block as a deliberate tribute.

Uniswap v2 introduced TWAP oracles by storing cumulative price sums each block. The design made on-chain price manipulation expensive by requiring an attacker to hold a distorted price across many consecutive blocks.
On this date in 2015, Microsoft's ResNet-152 surpassed human-level accuracy on ImageNet — 96.43% vs. 94.9% — ending a benchmark that had anchored computer vision research for five years.
On this date in 2022, Meta released OPT-175B's full weights publicly, the first time a GPT-3-scale model was open to researchers outside a major lab.
Training GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — roughly the annual usage of 4,500 U.S. homes — for a single pre-training run.
The 2024 AlphaFold 3 paper predicted the structures of protein-ligand complexes, a problem medicinal chemists had spent careers on, using a diffusion model trained without explicit physics.
Backpropagation was first applied to neural networks in 1986, but the algorithm itself was independently derived at least four times across different fields before that.
